tldr: China Daily first reported on Aug 6 that DeepSeek planned to raise its AI service prices, and CITIC Securities analysts treated the plan as confirmed days later, framing it as part of a broader trend of Chinese labs pushing larger models at higher prices. By Aug 10, coverage was describing the move as DeepSeek entering a more ambitious, costlier era.
whats_new: DeepSeek shipped V4-Pro on its API on Aug 13 with sharply higher user prices, confirming the reported hike, and released an open-source coding harness the same day positioned as a Claude Code rival.
why_it_matters: Teams running production workloads on DeepSeek's API for its low per-token cost should expect that cost advantage to narrow with V4-Pro and re-check budgets before the next bill.

status.detail: Weeks of reports and analyst notes about a coming DeepSeek price increase were confirmed when V4-Pro shipped on the API at sharply higher user prices.

V4-Pro ships at sharply higher API prices, alongside an open-source coding harness
beats.summary: The reported plan becomes a shipped price change the same day DeepSeek launches a Claude Code-rival tool.

open_questions: What are DeepSeek's new per-token API prices for V4-Pro compared to the prior tier?
Does the increase apply only to the hosted API, or also to open-weight model access?
How does the new DeepSeek Harness's pricing and licensing compare to Claude Code for teams evaluating a switch?
take_for_builders: Re-check DeepSeek API cost assumptions against V4-Pro's new pricing before it hits production spend, and evaluate whether the new open-source Harness offers a cheaper self-hosted path for coding-agent workloads.
